claims.text: PostgreSQL's default transaction isolation level is Read Committed; SHOW transaction_isolation prints 'read committed' in a session that asks for no other level.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.2 Transaction Isolation ('Read Committed is the default'); default_transaction_isolation; outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/lost-update.txt

claims.text: Under Read Committed a SELECT sees only data committed before the query began, never uncommitted changes of concurrent transactions; two SELECTs in one transaction can see different data.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.2.1 Read Committed Isolation Level

claims.text: Under Read Committed an UPDATE that finds the target row already updated by a concurrent uncommitted transaction waits; if that one commits, the UPDATE re-checks its WHERE on the updated row and, if it still matches, applies its change to it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.2.1 Read Committed Isolation Level (UPDATE, DELETE ... will wait for the first updating transaction)

claims.text: An UPDATE takes a row lock on the rows it changes, held until the transaction ends; a second UPDATE of the same row waits for it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.3.2 Row-Level Locks (FOR NO KEY UPDATE is acquired by any UPDATE that does not acquire a FOR UPDATE lock; Table 13.3)

claims.text: SaveChanges applies its changes in a transaction EF Core starts without naming a level; Npgsql then begins it as READ COMMITTED explicitly, so it runs under Read Committed even if the database default is changed.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Transactions, Default transaction behavior; live Npgsql 10.0.3 test (technical review round 1)

claims.text: The repository's FindAsync is a query that runs before SaveChangesAsync and outside the transaction SaveChangesAsync uses, unless code opens one with Database.BeginTransactionAsync first; that method has an overload taking an IsolationLevel.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Transactions, Controlling transactions; RelationalDatabaseFacadeExtensions.BeginTransactionAsync(IsolationLevel); EfOrderRepository.cs @ stage-2

claims.text: Under Repeatable Read all statements of a transaction see a snapshot as of its first query; an UPDATE of a row changed by a transaction that committed after that snapshot fails with 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update'.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.2.2 Repeatable Read Isolation Level

claims.text: The serialization failure has SQLSTATE 40001 (serialization_failure); applications using Repeatable Read must be prepared to retry the whole transaction.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.2.2 Repeatable Read; 13.4 Serialization Failure Handling; Appendix A Error Codes 40001

claims.text: CancelOrderAsync/ShipOrderAsync call FindAsync, then Cancel()/Ship() check the status in C#, then SaveChangesAsync; nothing re-reads the status between, and a re-read just before the save would still leave a gap before the write.
Cancel() on a shipped order throws OrderStatusException already-shipped, which the API answers with 409 and a type ending in already-shipped; the ship endpoint requires the StaffOnly policy.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: Entities.cs:83-88, OrdersController.cs:86-97; prereqs backend.l2.problem-types, backend.l2.role-based-access

claims.text: At stage-2 Order.Version is a concurrency token (IsRowVersion, xmin), so the real endpoints' second save fails and they do not lose this update; the scripts leave that guard out and use plain psql sessions.

lost-update.sh: ship session in background, cancel 0.5 s later, both read paid, both UPDATE 1, order 5 ends cancelled; the script resets order 5 to paid. repeatable-read-conflict.sh prints the 40001 error and order 5 ends shipped.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: scripts/backend/lost-update.sh, repeatable-read-conflict.sh; outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/*.txt; live run 2026-09-28

claims.text: After a serialization failure, running the whole cancel transaction again reads 'shipped', so Cancel() refuses it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.4 Serialization Failure Handling; Entities.cs:83-88 @ stage-2
